title: JSON.parse silently rounds a 64-bit id to the nearest value a JS number can hold
assumption: Parsing a JSON number and then stringifying it again gives back the exact same digits you started with.

input.display: JSON.parse("9007199254740993")  (a Twitter/Discord/Snowflake-style 64-bit id, one more than Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
input.description: Any API that returns large integer ids as bare JSON numbers (not strings) -- Twitter/X status ids, Discord snowflakes, some database auto-increment ids -- consumed by a JavaScript client.

what_goes_wrong: An id of 9007199254740993 round-trips through `JSON.parse` as 9007199254740992 -- a different, smaller, EVEN number -- so looking that id up, comparing it, or sending it back to the server can silently hit the wrong record or none at all.
why: The JSON specification defines numbers as an abstract decimal value with no size limit, but JavaScript's `JSON.parse` converts every JSON number into a 64-bit double, which (per IEEE 754) represents every integer exactly only up to 2^53; above that, neighbouring integers start sharing a double, which is why 2^53 - 1 is the largest 'safe' integer. 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1) has no exact double representation; the nearest one is 2^53 (9007199254740992), and ties-to-even rounding picks that over 2^53 + 2. This is exactly why large-id APIs increasingly send such ids as JSON strings instead of bare numbers.

repros.code:
import json

# Python's json module parses integers into arbitrary-precision int, so no
# precision is lost here -- the gotcha is specific to a 64-bit-double parser.
id_value = json.loads("9007199254740993")
print(id_value, id_value == 9007199254740993)

fix: Never transmit an id that could exceed 2^53 - 1 as a bare JSON number; encode it as a JSON string on the wire, and parse/compare it as a string or BigInt on the JavaScript side, never as a plain `number`. If you cannot change the wire format, V8-based runtimes (Node 22, recent Chrome) pass the raw source text to a reviver as a third argument: `JSON.parse(text, (k, v, ctx) => typeof v === 'number' && !Number.isSafeInteger(v) ? BigInt(ctx.source) : v)`.

sources.title: RFC 8259: The JSON Data Interchange Format (numbers have no size limit)

test_cases.note: Parsing a large id from JSON must not silently change its value; compare as string or BigInt.
